references.text: Aaron and his sons shall take care of their priestly service. If a stranger approaches, he must die. This establishes the principle that only Aaron's descendants may serve as priests.
The censers were beaten into plates as a reminder for the Israelites, so that no stranger who is not of Aaron's line should approach to burn incense before the Lord.
The priestly service is given as a gift to Aaron and his sons, and any stranger who approaches must die.
Korah's rebellion, in which he and his followers challenged Aaron's priesthood and demanded the right to burn incense.
The judgment against Korah and his followers, where the earth swallowed them and fire consumed the 250 men who offered incense.
Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on the altar every morning and evening – this is the legitimate incense service reserved for Aaron's priesthood.
Nadab and Abihu brought unauthorized fire before the Lord and died. An example of an unauthorised approach to the Lord's sanctuary.
King Uzziah attempted to burn incense in the temple even though he was not a priest, and was struck with leprosy as punishment.
No one takes this honor upon himself, but is called by God, just as Aaron. This confirms the principle of divine selection for the priesthood.
